      requestAnimationFrame(() => step(n - 1));
    };
    step(count);
  });

  const requiredFonts = [
    "300 16px 'Inter Variable'",
    "450 16px 'Inter Variable'",
    "600 16px 'Inter Variable'",
    "750 16px 'Inter Variable'",
    "900 16px 'Inter Variable'",
    "300 16px 'Inter'",
    "600 16px 'Inter'",
    "900 16px 'Inter'",
  ];
  await Promise.all(requiredFonts.map((d) => document.fonts.load(d, 'BESbswy')));
  await document.fonts.ready;
  await waitFrames(2);

  return await new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    try {
      const logs: any[] = [];
      new (window as any).p5((p: any) => {
        p.setup = () => {
          p.pixelDensity(1);
          p.createCanvas(1160, 350);
          p.noLoop();
        };

        p.draw = () => {
          try {
            const weights = [300, 450, 600, 750, 900];
            const maybeTextWeight = p.textWeight;

            // Simulate first family loop end state
            p.textFont('Inter');
            p.textSize(30);
            p.textStyle(p.NORMAL);
            for (const w of weights) p.textWeight(w);
            p.textStyle(p.BOLD);
            p.text('BOLD style control', 24, 280);
            p.textStyle(p.NORMAL);
            p.textSize(16);
            p.text('support line', 24, 314);
            p.text('width line', 24, 334);

            // Second family as in sketch
            p.textFont('Inter Variable');
            p.textSize(30);
            p.textStyle(p.NORMAL);

            for (const w of weights) {
              p.textStyle(p.NORMAL);
              maybeTextWeight.call(p, w);
              const tw = p.textWidth('The quick brown fox');
              const fw = p.fontWidth('The quick brown fox');
              logs.push({
                phase: 'loop',
                w,
                textWeightGetter: p.textWeight(),
                font: p.drawingContext.font,
                fvs: p.canvas.style.fontVariationSettings,
                tw,
                fw,
              });
              p.text(`w${w}  The quick brown fox`, 590, 60 + (weights.indexOf(w) * 44));
            }

            resolve(logs);
          } catch (err) {
            reject(err);
          }
        };
      }, document.body);
    } catch (err) {
      reject(err);
    }
  });
});

console.log(JSON.stringify(result, null, 2));
await client.disconnect();
EOF

        }

        out.pOwnHasTextWeight = Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(p, "textWeight");
        out.pTextWeightChanged = p.textWeight !== origP;
        out.rTextWeightChanged = renderer.textWeight !== origR;
        out.callP = p.textWeight(300);
        out.callR = renderer.textWeight(300);
        done(true);
      };
      p.draw = () => {};
    });

    setTimeout(() => fail(new Error("timeout")), 8000);
  });
  return out;
});

import { NativeTextEngine } from "./apps/deno-notebooks/tools/p5gpu_text/ffi.ts";

const engine = new NativeTextEngine();
const text = "The quick brown fox";
const weights = [300, 450, 600, 750, 900];

function tightFromRaster(layout) {
  let minLeft = Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY;
  let maxRight = Number.NEGATIVE_INFINITY;
  for (const glyph of layout.glyphs) {
    const g = engine.rasterizeGlyph(glyph.key);
    if (!g || g.width <= 0 || g.height <= 0) continue;
    const left = glyph.x + g.left;
    const right = left + g.width;
    if (left < minLeft) minLeft = left;
    if (right > maxRight) maxRight = right;
  }
  if (!Number.isFinite(minLeft) || !Number.isFinite(maxRight)) return 0;
  return Math.max(0, maxRight - minLeft);
}

for (const family of ["Inter Variable", "Roboto Flex"]) {
  const vals400: string[] = [];
  const valsWeight: string[] = [];
  for (const w of weights) {
    const layoutA = engine.layoutText({
      text, family, fontSize: 30, lineHeight: 38.25, width: null, height: null,
      alignH: 0, wrapMode: 2, weight: 400, style: 0, axisQuantization: 1, axes: { wght: w },
    });
    const layoutB = engine.layoutText({
      text, family, fontSize: 30, lineHeight: 38.25, width: null, height: null,
      alignH: 0, wrapMode: 2, weight: w, style: 0, axisQuantization: 1, axes: { wght: w },
    });
    vals400.push(`${w}:${tightFromRaster(layoutA).toFixed(1)}`);
    valsWeight.push(`${w}:${tightFromRaster(layoutB).toFixed(1)}`);
  }
  console.log(`\n${family}`);
  console.log(`weight=400 axes=wght ${vals400.join('  ')}`);
  console.log(`weight=w   axes=wght ${valsWeight.join('  ')}`);
}
engine.dispose();
EOF

import { NativeTextEngine } from "./apps/deno-notebooks/tools/p5gpu_text/ffi.ts";

const engine = new NativeTextEngine();
const text = "The quick brown fox";

function tightWidth(family:string, w:number) {
  const res = engine.layoutText({
    text,
    family,
    fontSize:30,
    lineHeight:38.25,
    width:null,
    height:null,
    alignH:0,
    wrapMode:2,
    weight:w,
    style:0,
    axisQuantization:1,
    axes:{wght:w},
  });
  // compute mask-tight like p5gpu
  let min = Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY;
  let max = Number.NEGATIVE_INFINITY;
  for (const glyph of res.glyphs) {
    const g = engine.rasterizeGlyph(glyph.key);
    if (!g) continue;
    const l = glyph.x + g.left;
    const r = l + g.width;
    if (l < min) min = l;
    if (r > max) max = r;
  }
  if (!Number.isFinite(min) || !Number.isFinite(max)) return 0;
  return max - min;
}

const targets = [259.5,268.7,276.3,284.5,294.4];
const css = [300,450,600,750,900];

for (const family of ["Inter Variable","Roboto Flex"]) {
  console.log("\n", family);
  const table: Array<[number,number]> = [];
  for (let w=1; w<=1000; w+=1) {
    table.push([w, tightWidth(family,w)]);
  }
  for (let i=0;i<css.length;i++) {
    const t = family === "Inter Variable" ? targets[i] : [244.2,251.1,266.7,282.3,298.2][i];
    let bestW = -1;
    let bestErr = 1e9;
    let bestWidth = 0;
    for (const [w,tw] of table) {
      const err = Math.abs(tw - t);
      if (err < bestErr) { bestErr = err; bestW = w; bestWidth = tw; }
    }
    console.log(`target css${css[i]} width ${t} -> native weight ${bestW} width ${bestWidth.toFixed(1)} err ${bestErr.toFixed(1)}`);
  }
}
engine.dispose();
EOF

I found a likely root cause on the browser reference side: variable fonts are injected as `format('truetype')`, which can cause variable-axis handling inconsistencies in Chrome data-URL font faces. **Conclusion**
- The browser baseline is now behaving consistently.
- Remaining gap is in the native text path for variable-font shaping/metrics (not a browser race anymore).
- This aligns with known rough edges in cosmic-text around variable-axis handling/matching (`TODO: correctly take variable axes into account` in font matching logic, and related issue discussion: https://github.com/pop-os/cosmic-text/issues/406).

         let data: Arc<Vec<u8>> = Arc::new(bytes.to_vec());
         let source: Arc<dyn AsRef<[u8]> + Send + Sync> = data;
         self.font_system
             .db_mut()
             .load_font_source(fontdb::Source::Binary(source));
+        self.prune_static_instances_for_variable_families();
     }
+
+    fn prune_static_instances_for_variable_families(&mut self) {
+        #[derive(Clone)]
+        struct FaceScan {
+            id: fontdb::ID,
+            families: Vec<String>,
+            signature: (usize, usize, u32),
+            has_variations: bool,
+        }
+
+        let db = self.font_system.db();
+        let face_ids: Vec<fontdb::ID> = db.faces().map(|face| face.id).collect();
+        if face_ids.len() < 2 {
+            return;
+        }
+
+        let mut scans = Vec::<FaceScan>::with_capacity(face_ids.len());
+        for id in face_ids {
+            let Some(face) = db.face(id) else {
+                continue;
+            };
+
+            let families = face
+                .families
+                .iter()
+                .map(|(name, _)| name.clone())
+                .collect::<Vec<_>>();
+
+            let scan_opt = db.with_face_data(id, |font_data, face_index| {
+                let ptr = font_data.as_ptr() as usize;
+                let len = font_data.len();
+                let has_variations = swash::FontRef::from_index(font_data, face_index as usize)
+                    .ok()
+                    .and_then(|font_ref| {
+                        let wght = swash::Tag::from_be_bytes(*b"wght");
+                        let wdth = swash::Tag::from_be_bytes(*b"wdth");
+                        let opsz = swash::Tag::from_be_bytes(*b"opsz");
+                        Some(
+                            font_ref.variations().find_by_tag(wght).is_some()
+                                || font_ref.variations().find_by_tag(wdth).is_some()
+                                || font_ref.variations().find_by_tag(opsz).is_some(),
+                        )
+                    })
+                    .unwrap_or(false);
+
+                FaceScan {
+                    id,
+                    families,
+                    signature: (ptr, len, face_index),
+                    has_variations,
+                }
+            });
+
+            if let Some(scan) = scan_opt {
+                scans.push(scan);
+            }
+        }
+
+        if scans.len() < 2 {
+            return;
+        }
+
+        let mut variable_signatures_by_family: HashMap<String, HashSet<(usize, usize, u32)>> =
+            HashMap::new();
+        for scan in &scans {
+            if !scan.has_variations {
+                continue;
+            }
+            for family in &scan.families {
+                variable_signatures_by_family
+                    .entry(family.clone())
+                    .or_default()
+                    .insert(scan.signature);
+            }
+        }
+
+        if variable_signatures_by_family.is_empty() {
+            return;
+        }
+
+        let mut remove_ids = Vec::<fontdb::ID>::new();
+        for scan in &scans {
+            if scan.has_variations {
+                continue;
+            }
+            let should_remove = scan.families.iter().any(|family| {
+                variable_signatures_by_family
+                    .get(family)
+                    .map(|signatures| signatures.contains(&scan.signature))
+                    .unwrap_or(false)
+            });
+            if should_remove {
+                remove_ids.push(scan.id);
+            }
+        }
+
+        if remove_ids.is_empty() {
+            return;
+        }
+
+        let db_mut = self.font_system.db_mut();
+        for id in remove_ids {
+            db_mut.remove_face(id);
+        }
+
+        self.glyph_records.clear();
+        self.axis_image_cache.clear();
+    }

use cosmic_text::fontdb;
use std::fs;
use std::path::PathBuf;

fn main() {
    let root = PathBuf::from(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"))
        .join("..")
        .join("..")
        .join("assets")
        .join("fonts");

    let mut db = fontdb::Database::new();

    for name in [
        "NotoSans-Regular.ttf",
        "Inter-Regular.ttf",
        "Inter-Bold.ttf",
        "InterVariable.ttf",
        "InterVariable-Italic.ttf",
        "RobotoFlex-Variable.ttf",
    ] {
        let path = root.join(name);
        let bytes = fs::read(&path).expect("read font");
        let arc: std::sync::Arc<dyn AsRef<[u8]> + Send + Sync> = std::sync::Arc::new(bytes);
        let ids = db.load_font_source(fontdb::Source::Binary(arc));
        println!("loaded {name} => {} face(s)", ids.len());
    }

    println!("\nfaces in db: {}", db.len());

    for face in db.faces() {
        let family = face
            .families
            .iter()
            .map(|(f, _)| f.clone())
            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
            .join(" | ");
        let var_axes = db
            .with_face_data(face.id, |data, index| {
                swash::FontRef::from_index(data, index as usize)
                    .map(|fr| {
                        let tags = [
                            swash::Tag::from_be_bytes(*b"wght"),
                            swash::Tag::from_be_bytes(*b"wdth"),
                            swash::Tag::from_be_bytes(*b"opsz"),
                        ];
                        tags.into_iter()
                            .filter(|tag| fr.variations().find_by_tag(*tag).is_some())
                            .map(|tag| String::from_utf8_lossy(&tag.to_be_bytes()).to_string())
                            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
                    })
                    .unwrap_or_default()
            })
            .unwrap_or_default();

        println!(
            "id={:?} index={} family='{}' ps='{}' style={:?} weight={} var_axes={:?}",
            face.id,
            face.index,
            family,
            face.post_script_name,
            face.style,
            face.weight.0,
            var_axes,
        );
    }

    for fam in ["Inter", "Inter Variable", "Roboto Flex", "Noto Sans"] {
        for w in [300u16, 450, 600, 750, 900] {
            let q = fontdb::Query {
                families: &[fontdb::Family::Name(fam)],
                weight: fontdb::Weight(w),
                stretch: fontdb::Stretch::Normal,
                style: fontdb::Style::Normal,
            };
            let picked = db.query(&q);
            let picked_s = picked
                .and_then(|id| db.face(id))
                .map(|f| format!("id={:?} idx={} ps={} w={}", f.id, f.index, f.post_script_name, f.weight.0))
                .unwrap_or_else(|| "none".to_string());
            println!("query family='{fam}' weight={w} -> {picked_s}");
        }
        println!();
    }
}
EOF

### Agent

I’ll proceed in the order you asked: first fix on top of cosmic-text, then only if blocked I’ll evaluate replacing it with lower-level shaping/raster libs. I’m now inspecting what face cosmic/fontdb is actually selecting for `Inter Variable` and whether we can force variable-face selection without forking.

I found a concrete non-fork path: prune fontdb’s static named-instance faces when a variable face from the same source/family exists. This targets exactly the likely mismatch (fontdb picking named instances instead of true variable interpolation). I’m implementing that in our native `text_engine` layer now and then rebuilding for validation.

I’ve added the pruning fix in our native engine. Next I’m rebuilding `text_engine` and running the focused width probes (`NativeTextEngine` and then `text-weight-api-probe` browser-vs-webgpu) to see if this resolves the low-weight width mismatch.

Build failed on a small API mismatch (`swash::FontRef::from_index` returns `Option`, not `Result`). I’m patching that and rebuilding now.

I now have a direct HarfRust shaping probe compiled; next I’m measuring advances with and without `opsz` to verify whether non-`wght` axes materially change line width (which would confirm cosmic’s axis-limited shaping is the blocker).

### Agent

I reverted the no-hinting experiment (it didn’t help), kept the axis-aware advance bridge, and kept the browser patch that fixed the off-by-one/rotated weight baseline. I’m doing one clean re-run to capture the final comparison state.

Implemented the “fix on top of cosmic” first, then validated it.

**What I changed**
- `apps/deno-notebooks/native/text_engine/src/lib.rs`
  - Added a non-fork bridge that keeps cosmic layout/raster flow, but computes per-run advance using HarfRust with variation settings and applies an x-scale to glyph placement.
  - It auto-infers `opsz` from `font_size` when the font exposes `opsz` and no explicit `opsz` axis was provided.
  - This is algorithmic (not magic constants), and only kicks in when needed.
- `apps/deno-notebooks/libraryIntegrationTetsts/browser_render_references.ts`
  - Fixed browser reference `textWeight` patch to avoid one-step carryover by re-setting weight before each `_applyTextProperties()` pass.

**Validation**
- Ran:
  - `P5GPU_NAME_FILTER='text-weight-api-probe' P5GPU_MAX_PHASE=6 deno run -A libraryIntegrationTetsts/p5_browser_comparison_tests.ts`
- Latest run log:
  - `apps/deno-notebooks/.output/browser_analysis/run_2026-02-14T03-26-02-917Z_axis_scale_final_clean.json`
- Metrics moved from roughly:
  - `text-weight-api-probe`: `61.12 -> 58.72` RMSE
  - `text-weight-api-probe-alt-font`: `61.59 -> 56.89` RMSE
- Probe widths are now much closer:
  - Inter Variable webgpu now tracks browser monotonic weights closely (e.g. ~`260,269,276,284,295` vs browser ~`259.5,268.7,276.3,284.5,294.4`).

**Investigation outcome**
- A pure cosmic-only fix is still limited: cosmic shaping path does not expose full arbitrary variation-axis shaping control (`opsz`, etc.) in the way we need.
- Remaining diff is now mostly rasterization/AA style mismatch rather than gross weight-width mismatch.
- If you want the next step, I can proceed with deeper replacement of cosmic layout/shaping with underlying libs (fontdb + HarfRust path), while keeping the current raster path, and then evaluate if that materially reduces visual diff further.

## Turn 178 — 2026-02-14T03:37:21.404Z

### User

i just need a guestimate


### Agent

Guestimate: for variable-font text (Inter Variable / Roboto Flex), this change is roughly **an extra full shaping pass per laid-out run**, so the affected layout work is about **1.6x to 2.5x CPU** vs before.

For a single `text()` of a few hundred chars at 60fps, I’d expect roughly:

- **Desktop / fast laptop:** about **+0.3ms to +1.5ms per call**
- **Mid/older CPU:** about **+1ms to +3ms per call**

So if you do one big text block/frame, usually still fine. If you do many variable-font blocks per frame, it can eat frame budget quickly.

For non-variable fonts (or paths that skip this adjustment), impact is near zero.


---


## Turn 179 — 2026-02-14T03:38:46.960Z

### User

what about LFO style modulation of ~100 individual characters


### Agent

For **100 individually-modulated characters** (each character getting its own `text()`/weight update per frame), guestimate is:

- **Likely not 60fps-safe** with current path.
- Roughly **10–30 ms/frame CPU** on a decent desktop just for layout/shaping work.
- Can be **20–60+ ms/frame** on slower CPUs once glyph raster/upload churn is included.

Why: each char effectively pays near **2 shaping passes** (cosmic layout + HarfRust advance correction), and LFO weight changes can cause frequent glyph-cache misses.

If you quantize weight to a small number of bins (instead of continuous LFO), this drops a lot.

+

+const CHAR_COUNT = 100;
+
+const LOREM = (

+).slice(0, CHAR_COUNT);
+
+const CHARS = LOREM.split("");

+  let startX = 40;
+  let startY = 90;
+  let lastFrameTime = 0;
+  const frameTimes: number[] = [];
+  const drawTimes: number[] = [];
+
+  const pushSample = (arr: number[], v: number, maxSamples = LOG_EVERY): void => {
+    arr.push(v);
+    if (arr.length > maxSamples) arr.shift();
+  };
+
+  const avg = (arr: number[]): number => {
+    if (arr.length === 0) return 0;
+    let sum = 0;
+    for (const v of arr) sum += v;
+    return sum / arr.length;
+  };
+
+  const recomputeLayout = (): void => {
+    p.textFont("monospace");
+    p.textSize(36);
+    const sampleW = p.textWidth("M");
+    const sampleH = p.textAscent("M") + p.textDescent("M");
+    cellW = Math.max(1, Math.ceil(sampleW * 1.05));
+    cellH = Math.max(1, Math.ceil(sampleH * 1.35));
+    gridCols = Math.max(10, Math.floor((p.width - 80) / cellW));
+    const rows = Math.ceil(CHARS.length / gridCols);
+    startX = Math.floor((p.width - gridCols * cellW) * 0.5);
+    startY = Math.max(70, Math.floor((p.height - rows * cellH) * 0.4));
+  };
+
+  p.setup = () => {
+    p.createCanvas(WIDTH, HEIGHT);
+    p.pixelDensity(1);
+    p.noStroke();
+    p.textAlign(p.LEFT, p.TOP);
+    p.textWrap(p.CHAR);
+
+    supportsTextWeight = typeof p.textWeight === "function";
+    recomputeLayout();
+    lastFrameTime = performance.now();
+
+    console.log(
+      `[lfo-text-perf] start chars=${CHARS.length} font=monospace textWeight=${supportsTextWeight ? "yes" : "no"}`,
+    );
+    console.log(`[lfo-text-perf] logging running averages every ${LOG_EVERY} frames`);
+  };
+
+  p.draw = () => {
+    const drawStart = performance.now();
+    const frameNow = drawStart;
+    const frameMs = frameNow - lastFrameTime;
+    lastFrameTime = frameNow;
+    pushSample(frameTimes, frameMs);
+
+    p.background(15, 18, 26);
+    p.textFont("monospace");
+    p.textSize(36);
+    p.textStyle(p.NORMAL);
+
+    const t = frameNow * 0.001;
+    for (let i = 0; i < CHARS.length; i++) {
+      const ch = CHARS[i];
+      const col = i % gridCols;
+      const row = Math.floor(i / gridCols);
+      const x = startX + col * cellW;
+      const y = startY + row * cellH;
+
+      const lfo = 0.5 + 0.5 * Math.sin(t * 2.2 + i * 0.17);
+      const weight = Math.round(300 + lfo * 600);
+      if (supportsTextWeight) {
+        p.textWeight(weight);
+      } else {
+        p.textStyle(weight >= 650 ? p.BOLD : p.NORMAL);
+      }
+
+      const c = Math.round(170 + lfo * 70);
+      p.fill(c, c, c + 5);
+      p.text(ch, x, y);

+
+    if (supportsTextWeight) p.textWeight(400);

+    p.fill(138, 170, 255);
+    p.text(
+      "LFO weight modulation, manual monospace character layout",
+      24,
+      20,
+    );
+
+    const drawMs = performance.now() - drawStart;
+    pushSample(drawTimes, drawMs);
+
+    if (p.frameCount % LOG_EVERY === 0) {
+      const avgFrameMs = avg(frameTimes);
+      const avgDrawMs = avg(drawTimes);
+      const approxFps = avgFrameMs > 0 ? 1000 / avgFrameMs : 0;
+      console.log(
+        `[lfo-text-perf] frame=${String(p.frameCount).padStart(5)} avgFrameMs(${LOG_EVERY})=${avgFrameMs.toFixed(2)} avgDrawMs(${LOG_EVERY})=${avgDrawMs.toFixed(2)} fps≈${approxFps.toFixed(1)}`,
+      );
+    }
+  };
+}, {
+  width: WIDTH,
+  height: HEIGHT,
+  title: "p5 text LFO perf benchmark",
+});
+
+try {

+} finally {

+}
*** End Patch

+

+      `ctx.font=${snapshot.ctxFont}`,

+    );
+  };
+

+    const size = sizes[Math.floor(i / (families.length * weights.length)) % sizes.length];
+    const text = texts[Math.floor(i / (families.length * weights.length * sizes.length)) % texts.length];
+    const style = styles[Math.floor(i / (families.length * weights.length * sizes.length * texts.length)) % styles.length];
+
+    p.textFont(family);

+

+

+    const snapshot: ProbeSnapshot = {

+      );

+    drawProbe(recentBad ?? snapshot);

  - `Math.max(1, NaN)` is still `NaN`
  - then positions like `y = startY + row * cellH` become `NaN`, causing visual collapse/overlap.

I’ll inspect both sides: the window/blit helper path for size mismatches and the `p5_text_lfo_perf.ts` assumptions about metrics/layout. Then I’ll give you a concrete diagnosis of which assumption is wrong.

I found the exact mismatch bug: the blit shader computes UV from fragment pixel position divided by **source texture dimensions**, so when destination surface is larger (HiDPI/resize), UV exceeds 1.0 and clamps to edge, producing those “extended white lines.” I’m patching `window/blit.ts` now to use proper interpolated 0..1 UVs.

I’ve patched the blit mapping bug. I’ll do a quick run to confirm there are no shader/runtime regressions and then summarize whether the sketch itself has incorrect assumptions.

You were right: the sketch itself is not causing the “extended line” artifact in the window.

Root cause was in the blit helper, not `p5_text_lfo_perf.ts`:
- `apps/deno-notebooks/window/blit.ts` fragment shader was doing `uv = pos.xy / textureDimensions(src)`.
- When the window surface is larger than the source canvas texture (HiDPI/resize mismatch), UV goes > 1.0 and clamps to edge, which visually looks like lines stretching to the window edge.

I fixed it in `apps/deno-notebooks/window/blit.ts`:
- Blit shader now passes proper interpolated 0..1 UV from vertex to fragment and samples with that.
- This removes edge-extension from source/destination size mismatch.

I reran `p5_text_lfo_perf.ts` with frame-10 snapshot capture successfully after the fix.  
If you want, next step is adding letterbox/pillarbox mode so it preserves aspect ratio instead of scaling-to-fill.

### Agent

Diagnosis from the image: this is an atlas invalidation artifact, not a metrics/layout bug.

What I see in `p5gpu` image:
- Early rows (top, drawn first) are shredded/partial.
- Later rows (lower, drawn later) are much more coherent.

That pattern matches mid-frame glyph atlas rebuild:
- `ensureGlyph()` can trigger grow/clear while text quads are already being accumulated (`apps/deno-notebooks/tools/p5gpu_text/atlas.ts:110`).
- On overflow it calls `_growTexture()` / `_clearAtlas()` (`apps/deno-notebooks/tools/p5gpu_text/atlas.ts:134`, `apps/deno-notebooks/tools/p5gpu_text/atlas.ts:195`, `apps/deno-notebooks/tools/p5gpu_text/atlas.ts:219`).
- `_growTexture()` destroys/recreates the texture and clears entries (`apps/deno-notebooks/tools/p5gpu_text/atlas.ts:202`, `apps/deno-notebooks/tools/p5gpu_text/atlas.ts:212`).
- Previously emitted UVs then point to stale/empty/wrong atlas content, so earlier-drawn glyphs look broken.

This also matches your run stats (`grows=1`) for that sketch.

So the core issue is: atlas growth/clear during a frame invalidates already-emitted text vertices.

## Turn 201 — 2026-02-14T04:47:10.610Z

### User

why does this happen - is it a race condition


### Agent

Not a thread race condition. It’s a deterministic atlas invalidation bug.

What happens:
1. In one frame, you draw many glyphs with many different `textWeight` values.
2. That creates lots of unique glyph keys (same character at different weights = different atlas entries).
3. Mid-frame, atlas allocation overflows and triggers grow/clear.
4. Quads emitted earlier in the frame keep UVs for old atlas content, but by render time the atlas texture has been replaced/cleared, so those quads sample wrong pixels.

Why it looks “random”:
- Early text gets corrupted most (it was queued before atlas rebuild).
- Later text looks better (queued after rebuild).

So: it’s a frame-lifetime/invalidation issue, not async timing between threads.

### Agent

I found another likely deterministic fault: we were destroying the old atlas texture immediately after submitting the GPU copy during growth. If the copy hasn’t completed yet, old glyph data can become invalid. I’m patching atlas growth to defer destruction until submitted work completes.

I’ve applied a safer grow lifecycle (deferred old-texture destruction). I’m rerunning the same single-sketch comparison to verify whether this removes the broken glyph fragments.

### Agent

I’ve added targeted growth logging and will run the same test once with `P5_TEXT_ATLAS_GROW_DEBUG=1` to confirm exactly when growth occurs relative to emitted vertices.

I found the deterministic root cause in the test harness: it draws each sketch twice in the same frame (`beginFrame()` once, `draw()` twice), so the first-pass broken metric layout and second-pass layout are composited together. I’m fixing the harness to run warmup in separate frames, then capture a clean single frame.

I’m going to probe the `text-lfo-perf-frame0` draw numerically (computed `cellW/cellH/startY` and emitted text vertex Y ranges) so we can confirm whether this is a coordinate/layout issue versus glyph sampling corruption.

I just confirmed no growth log fired inside `text()`; next I’m directly logging atlas stats/size from the probe run to see exactly when growth happens and whether the corrupted render can occur even with no in-loop growth events.

import { P5GPU } from "../tools/p5gpu.ts";
import { requestWebGpuDevice } from "../libraryIntegrationTetsts/raw-webgpu-helpers.ts";
import { P5_TEST_SKETCHES } from "../libraryIntegrationTetsts/p5_test_sketches.ts";

function align(v: number, a: number): number { return Math.ceil(v / a) * a; }

async function readR8(device: GPUDevice, texture: GPUTexture, w: number, h: number): Promise<Uint8Array> {
  const bytesPerRow = align(w, 256);
  const buf = device.createBuffer({ size: bytesPerRow * h, usage: GPUBufferUsage.COPY_DST | GPUBufferUsage.MAP_READ });
  const enc = device.createCommandEncoder();
  enc.copyTextureToBuffer({ texture }, { buffer: buf, bytesPerRow, rowsPerImage: h }, { width: w, height: h, depthOrArrayLayers: 1 });
  device.queue.submit([enc.finish()]);
  await buf.mapAsync(GPUMapMode.READ);
  const mapped = new Uint8Array(buf.getMappedRange());
  const out = new Uint8Array(w * h);
  for (let y = 0; y < h; y++) {
    out.set(mapped.subarray(y * bytesPerRow, y * bytesPerRow + w), y * w);
  }
  buf.unmap();
  buf.destroy();
  return out;
}

const sketch = P5_TEST_SKETCHES.find((s) => s.name === "text-lfo-perf-frame0");
if (!sketch) throw new Error("missing sketch");
const device = await requestWebGpuDevice();
const p = new P5GPU(device, { width: sketch.width, height: sketch.height });
p.beginFrame();
sketch.draw(p as never);
const atlas = (p as unknown as { _textAtlas: { size: number; texture: GPUTexture; entries: Map<bigint, any> } | null })._textAtlas;
if (!atlas) throw new Error('no atlas');
console.log('atlas size', atlas.size, 'entry count', atlas.entries.size, 'stats', p.textStats());
const entries = Array.from(atlas.entries.values()) as Array<{x:number;y:number;width:number;height:number;left:number;top:number;u0:number;v0:number;u1:number;v1:number;key:bigint}>;
entries.sort((a,b)=> (a.y-b.y) || (a.x-b.x));
for (const e of entries.slice(0, 16)) {
  console.log('entry', {x:e.x,y:e.y,w:e.width,h:e.height,left:e.left,top:e.top,u0:e.u0,v0:e.v0,u1:e.u1,v1:e.v1,key:e.key.toString(16)});
}

const atlasPixels = await readR8(device, atlas.texture, atlas.size, atlas.size);

function inspectEntry(e: {x:number;y:number;width:number;height:number}) {
  const rowSums: number[] = [];
  for (let yy=0; yy<e.height; yy++) {
    let sum = 0;
    for (let xx=0; xx<e.width; xx++) {
      sum += atlasPixels[(e.y + yy) * atlas.size + (e.x + xx)];
    }
    rowSums.push(sum);
  }
  const nonZeroRows = rowSums.map((s,i)=>({s,i})).filter((r)=>r.s>0);
  console.log('inspect', {x:e.x,y:e.y,w:e.width,h:e.height,nonZeroRows: nonZeroRows.slice(0,6), nonZeroRowsTail: nonZeroRows.slice(-6)});
}

const firstRowEntries = entries.filter((e)=>e.y===0).slice(0,8);
for (const e of firstRowEntries) inspectEntry(e);

p.endFrame();
p.dispose();
device.destroy();

### Agent

Yes. I fixed the deterministic corruption.

What was wrong:
- Atlas growth was happening during `text()` calls, but some growth happened in the pre-draw measurement path (`_measureTextBlockTightWidth`) and invalidated UV assumptions for already-buffered glyph vertices.

What I changed:
- In `text()` I now detect atlas size changes both:
  - after pre-draw tight-width probing, and
  - during glyph `ensureGlyph` in the draw loop,
  and rescale already-buffered UVs accordingly.
  - `apps/deno-notebooks/tools/p5gpu.ts:995`
  - `apps/deno-notebooks/tools/p5gpu.ts:2855`
- I also skip tight-width probing for the common left-aligned draw path (uses `layout.tightWidth` directly), which avoids unnecessary glyph atlas churn.
  - `apps/deno-notebooks/tools/p5gpu.ts:1016`
- Atlas growth now:
  - copies old texture into the new texture,
  - recomputes entry UVs for the new atlas size,
  - defers destroying the old texture until submitted GPU work is done.
  - `apps/deno-notebooks/tools/p5gpu_text/atlas.ts:200`
  - `apps/deno-notebooks/tools/p5gpu_text/atlas.ts:291`

   private _resolvedTextAxes(resolvedWeight: number): Record<string, number> {
     const axes: Record<string, number> = { ...this._state.textAxes };
     if (this._state.textWeightSet && !Number.isFinite(axes.wght)) {
       // p5 v2 textWeight() updates the active weight axis when available.
       axes.wght = resolvedWeight;
     }
     return axes;
   }
+
+  private _resolvedFontBoxMetrics(
+    layout: Pick<TextLayoutResult, "ascent" | "descent" | "fontAscent" | "fontDescent">,
+  ): { ascent: number; descent: number } {
+    const ascent = Number.isFinite(layout.fontAscent) && layout.fontAscent > 0
+      ? layout.fontAscent
+      : Math.max(0, layout.ascent);
+    const descent = Number.isFinite(layout.fontDescent) && layout.fontDescent >= 0
+      ? layout.fontDescent
+      : Math.max(0, layout.descent);
+    return { ascent, descent };
+  }
+
+  private _textBaselineShift(
+    fontMetrics: { ascent: number; descent: number },
+  ): number {
+    switch (this._state.textAlignV) {
+      case "top":
+        return -fontMetrics.ascent;
+      case "bottom":
+        return fontMetrics.descent;
+      case "center":
+        return (fontMetrics.descent - fontMetrics.ascent) * 0.5;
+      case "alphabetic":
+      default:
+        return 0;
+    }
+  }

const device = await requestWebGpuDevice();
const p = new P5GPU(device, { width: 400, height: 200 });
p.beginFrame();

p.textSize(40);
p.textAlign(p.LEFT, p.TOP);

  maybeTextWeight.call(p, 400);

};

  descent: raw.descent,

  textDescentg: p.textDescent("g"),

  fontWidthPhrase: p.fontWidth("The quick brown fox"),

  layoutPhrase: pick(rawPhrase),
};

import { requestWebGpuDevice } from "../libraryIntegrationTetsts/raw-webgpu-helpers.ts";
import { P5GPU } from "../tools/p5gpu.ts";

const device = await requestWebGpuDevice();
const p = new P5GPU(device, { width: 400, height: 200 });
p.beginFrame();
p.textFont("Inter Variable");
p.textSize(40);
const maybeTextWeight = (p as unknown as { textWeight?: (weight: number) => unknown }).textWeight;
if (typeof maybeTextWeight === "function") maybeTextWeight.call(p, 400);
const rows: unknown[] = [];
for (const v of [p.TOP, p.BASELINE, p.BOTTOM, p.CENTER]) {
  p.textAlign(p.LEFT, v);
  rows.push({
    align: String(v),
    textWidthM: p.textWidth("M"),
    textAscentMg: p.textAscent("Mg"),
    textDescentg: p.textDescent("g"),
    fontAscent: p.fontAscent(),
    fontDescent: p.fontDescent(),
  });
}
console.log(JSON.stringify(rows, null, 2));
p.dispose();
device.destroy();

import { NativeTextEngine } from './tools/p5gpu_text/ffi.ts';

function measure(engine: NativeTextEngine, text: string, th: number) {
  const layout = engine.layoutText({
    text,
    family: 'Inter Variable',
    fontSize: 40,
    lineHeight: 51,
    width: null,
    height: null,
    alignH: 0,
    wrapMode: 2,
    weight: 400,
    style: 0,
    axisQuantization: 1,
    axes: { wght: 400 },
  });
  let minX = Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY;
  let maxX = Number.NEGATIVE_INFINITY;
  let minTop = Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY;
  let maxBottom = Number.NEGATIVE_INFINITY;
  for (const glyph of layout.glyphs) {
    const r = engine.rasterizeGlyph(glyph.key);
    if (!r) continue;
    const { width, height, left, top, pixels } = r;
    let gMinX = width, gMinY = height, gMaxX = -1, gMaxY = -1;
    for (let y = 0; y < height; y++) {
      for (let x = 0; x < width; x++) {
        const a = pixels[y * width + x] ?? 0;
        if (a >= th) {
          if (x < gMinX) gMinX = x;
          if (x > gMaxX) gMaxX = x;
          if (y < gMinY) gMinY = y;
          if (y > gMaxY) gMaxY = y;
        }
      }
    }
    if (gMaxX < gMinX || gMaxY < gMinY) continue;
    const leftAbs = glyph.x + left + gMinX;
    const rightAbs = glyph.x + left + (gMaxX + 1);
    const topAbs = glyph.y - top + gMinY;
    const botAbs = glyph.y - top + (gMaxY + 1);
    minX = Math.min(minX, leftAbs);
    maxX = Math.max(maxX, rightAbs);
    minTop = Math.min(minTop, topAbs);
    maxBottom = Math.max(maxBottom, botAbs);
  }
  if (!Number.isFinite(minX)) return null;
  const baseline = layout.firstBaseline > 0 ? layout.firstBaseline : layout.ascent;
  return {
    width: +(maxX - minX).toFixed(3),
    ascent: +(baseline - minTop).toFixed(3),
    descent: +(maxBottom - baseline).toFixed(3),
  };
}

const engine = new NativeTextEngine();
for (const th of [1, 64, 96, 112, 128, 144, 160, 176, 192]) {
  const m = measure(engine, 'M', th);
  const mg = measure(engine, 'Mg', th);
  const g = measure(engine, 'g', th);
  console.log(`th=${th}`, { M: m, Mg: mg, g });
}
engine.dispose();
TS

function tightWidth(engine: NativeTextEngine, text: string, th: number) {
  const layout = engine.layoutText({
    text, family: 'Inter Variable', fontSize: 30, lineHeight: 38.25,
    width: null, height: null, alignH: 0, wrapMode: 2, weight: 300, style: 0,
    axisQuantization: 1, axes: { wght: 300 },
  });
  let minX = Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY;
  let maxX = Number.NEGATIVE_INFINITY;
  for (const glyph of layout.glyphs) {
    const r = engine.rasterizeGlyph(glyph.key);
    if (!r) continue;
    let gMinX = r.width, gMaxX = -1;
    for (let y = 0; y < r.height; y++) {
      for (let x = 0; x < r.width; x++) {
        if ((r.pixels[y * r.width + x] ?? 0) >= th) {
          if (x < gMinX) gMinX = x;
          if (x > gMaxX) gMaxX = x;
        }
      }
    }
    if (gMaxX < gMinX) continue;
    const leftAbs = glyph.x + r.left + gMinX;
    const rightAbs = glyph.x + r.left + (gMaxX + 1);
    minX = Math.min(minX, leftAbs);
    maxX = Math.max(maxX, rightAbs);
  }
  if (!Number.isFinite(minX)) return 0;
  return +(maxX - minX).toFixed(3);
}

### Agent

It’s not a center-origin coordinate system. In this sketch the origin is still top-left.

What you’re seeing is a useful diagnostic signal: `x` drift crossing near center strongly suggests a **cell-width scale mismatch**, not a fixed anchor offset.

In `apps/deno-notebooks/libraryIntegrationTetsts/p5_test_sketches.ts:693` and `apps/deno-notebooks/libraryIntegrationTetsts/p5_test_sketches.ts:702`:

- `startX = floor((p.width - cols * cellW) * 0.5)`
- `x = startX + col * cellW`

If browser and WebGPU have different `cellW`, they also compute different `startX`; the error becomes approximately:
`x_error(col) ≈ (col - cols/2) * ΔcellW`

So error is near zero in the middle and grows toward left/right edges.  
That pattern is exactly what helps debug this: it points at `textWidth("M")`/metric drift rather than a general alignment-origin bug.

import { P5GPU } from "../tools/p5gpu.ts";
import { requestWebGpuDevice } from "../libraryIntegrationTetsts/raw-webgpu-helpers.ts";

function align(v: number, a: number): number { return Math.ceil(v / a) * a; }

async function readR8(device: GPUDevice, texture: GPUTexture, w: number, h: number): Promise<Uint8Array> {
  const bytesPerRow = align(w, 256);
  const buf = device.createBuffer({ size: bytesPerRow * h, usage: GPUBufferUsage.COPY_DST | GPUBufferUsage.MAP_READ });
  const enc = device.createCommandEncoder();
  enc.copyTextureToBuffer({ texture }, { buffer: buf, bytesPerRow, rowsPerImage: h }, { width: w, height: h, depthOrArrayLayers: 1 });
  device.queue.submit([enc.finish()]);
  await buf.mapAsync(GPUMapMode.READ);
  const mapped = new Uint8Array(buf.getMappedRange());
  const out = new Uint8Array(w * h);
  for (let y = 0; y < h; y++) out.set(mapped.subarray(y * bytesPerRow, y * bytesPerRow + w), y * w);
  buf.unmap();
  buf.destroy();
  return out;
}

function boundsAtThreshold(alpha: Uint8Array, w: number, h: number, thr: number): { x0: number; x1: number; width: number } {
  let minX = w;
  let maxX = -1;
  for (let y = 0; y < h; y++) {
    const row = y * w;
    for (let x = 0; x < w; x++) {
      if (alpha[row + x] >= thr) {
        if (x < minX) minX = x;
        if (x > maxX) maxX = x;
      }
    }
  }
  if (maxX < minX) return { x0: 0, x1: 0, width: 0 };
  return { x0: minX, x1: maxX + 1, width: maxX - minX + 1 };
}

function fractionalEdge(alpha: Uint8Array, w: number, h: number): { left: number; right: number; width: number } {
  // Find first/last non-zero columns and use alpha-weighted edge interpolation.
  let minX = w;
  let maxX = -1;
  for (let y = 0; y < h; y++) {
    const row = y * w;
    for (let x = 0; x < w; x++) {
      if (alpha[row + x] > 0) {
        if (x < minX) minX = x;
        if (x > maxX) maxX = x;
      }
    }
  }
  if (maxX < minX) return { left: 0, right: 0, width: 0 };

  let leftMax = 0;
  let rightMax = 0;
  for (let y = 0; y < h; y++) {
    const row = y * w;
    leftMax = Math.max(leftMax, alpha[row + minX]);
    rightMax = Math.max(rightMax, alpha[row + maxX]);
  }

  const left = minX + (1 - leftMax / 255);
  const right = maxX + (rightMax / 255);
  return { left, right, width: right - left };
}

const device = await requestWebGpuDevice();
const p = new P5GPU(device, { width: 300, height: 200 });

for (const file of [
  "NotoSans-Regular.ttf",
  "Inter-Regular.ttf",
  "Inter-Bold.ttf",
  "InterVariable.ttf",
  "InterVariable-Italic.ttf",
  "RobotoFlex-Variable.ttf",
]) {
  await p.loadFont(new URL(`../assets/fonts/${file}`, import.meta.url));
}

const maybeTextWeight = (p as unknown as { textWeight?: (weight: number) => unknown }).textWeight;
p.textFont("Inter Variable");
p.textStyle(p.NORMAL);
p.textSize(40);
if (typeof maybeTextWeight === "function") maybeTextWeight.call(p, 400);

p.beginFrame();
p.text("M", 20, 60);

const atlas = (p as unknown as { _textAtlas: { size: number; texture: GPUTexture; entries: Map<bigint, {x:number;y:number;width:number;height:number;left:number;top:number;inkX0:number;inkX1:number}> } | null })._textAtlas;
if (!atlas) throw new Error("no atlas");

const entry = Array.from(atlas.entries.values())[0];
if (!entry) throw new Error("no glyph entry");

const pixels = await readR8(device, atlas.texture, atlas.size, atlas.size);
const glyph = new Uint8Array(entry.width * entry.height);
for (let y = 0; y < entry.height; y++) {
  const srcRow = (entry.y + y) * atlas.size + entry.x;
  glyph.set(pixels.subarray(srcRow, srcRow + entry.width), y * entry.width);
}

console.log("entry", {
  width: entry.width,
  height: entry.height,
  left: entry.left,
  top: entry.top,
  inkX0: entry.inkX0,
  inkX1: entry.inkX1,
  textWidthM: p.textWidth("M"),
  fontWidthM: p.fontWidth("M"),
});

for (const thr of [1, 64, 96, 112, 128, 144, 160, 176, 192, 208, 224]) {
  console.log("thr", thr, boundsAtThreshold(glyph, entry.width, entry.height, thr));
}
console.log("frac", fractionalEdge(glyph, entry.width, entry.height));

p.endFrame();
p.dispose();
device.destroy();
EOF

deno run --unstable-webgpu --unstable-ffi --allow-ffi --allow-read --allow-env --allow-write apps/deno-notebooks/.output/p5_glyph_bound_probe.ts
```

+    fn measure_glyph_outline_x_bounds(
+        &self,
+        scale_context: &mut swash::scale::ScaleContext,
+        font_id: fontdb::ID,
+        glyph_id: u16,
+        font_size: f32,
+        weight: u16,
+        axes: &[AxisSetting],

+        if !font_size.is_finite() || font_size <= 0.0 {
+            return None;
+        }
+
+        self.font_system
+            .db()
+            .with_face_data(font_id, |font_data, face_index| {
+                let font_ref = swash::FontRef::from_index(font_data, face_index as usize)?;
+                let variations = font_ref.variations();
+                let mut settings = Vec::<swash::Setting<f32>>::new();
+                let mut has_wght = false;
+                let mut has_opsz = false;
+
+                for axis in axes {
+                    let tag = swash::Tag::from_be_bytes(axis.tag);
+                    let Some(var_axis) = variations.find_by_tag(tag) else {
+                        continue;
+                    };
+                    let value = axis
+                        .value
+                        .clamp(var_axis.min_value(), var_axis.max_value());
+                    settings.push((tag, value).into());
+                    if axis.tag == *b"wght" {
+                        has_wght = true;
+                    } else if axis.tag == *b"opsz" {
+                        has_opsz = true;
+                    }
+                }
+
+                if !has_wght {
+                    let wght_tag = swash::Tag::from_be_bytes(*b"wght");
+                    if let Some(var_axis) = variations.find_by_tag(wght_tag) {
+                        let value = f32::from(weight)
+                            .clamp(var_axis.min_value(), var_axis.max_value());
+                        settings.push((wght_tag, value).into());
+                    }
+                }
+
+                if !has_opsz {
+                    let opsz_tag = swash::Tag::from_be_bytes(*b"opsz");
+                    if let Some(var_axis) = variations.find_by_tag(opsz_tag) {
+                        let value = font_size.clamp(var_axis.min_value(), var_axis.max_value());
+                        settings.push((opsz_tag, value).into());
+                    }
+                }
+
+                let mut scaler = scale_context
+                    .builder(font_ref)
+                    .size(font_size)
+                    .hint(false);
+                if !settings.is_empty() {
+                    scaler = scaler.variations(settings.into_iter());
+                }
+                let mut scaler = scaler.build();
+
+                let outline = scaler.scale_outline(glyph_id)?;
+                let bounds = outline.bounds();
+                if !bounds.min.x.is_finite()
+                    || !bounds.max.x.is_finite()
+                    || bounds.max.x <= bounds.min.x
+                {
+                    return None;
+                }
+                Some((bounds.min.x, bounds.max.x))
+            })
+            .flatten()

### Agent

Yes, agreed. I’ll now wire `textWidth()` to a fractional metric path from shaping/layout (not atlas pixels), then validate against the existing browser probes to see if the center-zero drift collapses.

I found the key structural issue in code: JS `textWidth()` is still using atlas alpha bounds, and glyph positions coming back from Rust are integer-quantized (`physical.x/y`), so the current width path is effectively pixel-grid based. I’m now checking if we can compute a true fractional ink width directly from shaping/font extents and expose that as a separate layout metric.

I’m implementing a concrete native fix now: compute `tight_width` from vector glyph outline bounds (fractional) during layout, with a per-layout glyph-bounds cache. Then I’ll switch TS `textWidth`/tight align paths to consume that native `layout.tightWidth` instead of atlas alpha scans.

I’ve landed the first pass: native `tight_width` now comes from vector outline bounds (fractional) instead of atlas pixels, and `p5gpu.ts` now uses `layout.tightWidth` for `textWidth` and tight alignment paths. Next I’m rebuilding and rerunning the focused browser comparison probes to see how much the drift drops.

Running the same focused browser comparisons (`text-anchor-weight-probe` + `text-lfo-perf-frame0`) now so we can directly compare before/after metrics and inspect updated images.

Native code compiles cleanly. I’m now running the focused browser test pass to compare before/after metrics and regenerate images for visual verification.

First pass made things worse on `text-lfo-perf-frame0` (RMSE rose to `59.58`), so I’m inspecting the generated browser/p5gpu/diff images plus the run JSON to isolate exactly which dimension moved in the wrong direction before adjusting again.

+fn outline_used_x_bounds(outline: &swash::scale::Outline) -> Option<(f32, f32)> {
+    let points = outline.points();
+    let mut point_i = 0usize;
+    let mut min_x = f32::INFINITY;
+    let mut max_x = f32::NEG_INFINITY;
+
+    for verb in outline.verbs() {
+        let consumed = match verb {
+            Verb::MoveTo | Verb::LineTo => 1usize,
+            Verb::QuadTo => 2usize,
+            Verb::CurveTo => 3usize,
+            Verb::Close => 0usize,
+        };
+
+        if consumed == 0 {
+            continue;
+        }
+
+        let end = point_i + consumed;
+        let Some(slice) = points.get(point_i..end) else {
+            break;
+        };
+        for point in slice {
+            min_x = min_x.min(point.x);
+            max_x = max_x.max(point.x);
+        }
+        point_i = end;
+    }
+
+    if !min_x.is_finite() || !max_x.is_finite() || max_x <= min_x {
+        None
+    } else {
+        Some((min_x, max_x))
+    }
+}

+use cosmic_text::harfrust;
+use std::path::PathBuf;

+fn main() {

+        .join("..")
+        .join("..")
+        .join("assets")
+        .join("fonts")
+        .join("InterVariable.ttf");
+    let data = std::fs::read(&font_path).expect("read InterVariable.ttf");
+
+    let hfont = harfrust::FontRef::from_index(&data, 0).expect("harfrust font");
+    let shaper_data = harfrust::ShaperData::new(&hfont);
+    let instance = harfrust::ShaperInstance::from_variations(
+        &hfont,
+        [
+            harfrust::Variation {
+                tag: harfrust::Tag::new(b"wght"),
+                value: 400.0,
+            },
+            harfrust::Variation {
+                tag: harfrust::Tag::new(b"opsz"),
+                value: 40.0,
+            },
+        ],
+    );
+    let shaper = shaper_data
+        .shaper(&hfont)
+        .instance(Some(&instance))
+        .point_size(Some(40.0))
+        .build();
+
+    let mut buffer = harfrust::UnicodeBuffer::new();
+    buffer.push_str("M");
+    buffer.set_direction(harfrust::Direction::LeftToRight);
+    buffer.guess_segment_properties();
+    let glyph_buffer = shaper.shape(buffer, &[]);
+
+    let infos = glyph_buffer.glyph_infos();
+    let positions = glyph_buffer.glyph_positions();
+    let upem = shaper.units_per_em().max(1) as f32;
+    println!("upem={upem}");
+    println!(
+        "glyph_count={} gid={} x_adv={} x_off={}",
+        infos.len(),

+        positions.first().map(|p| p.x_offset).unwrap_or_default()

+    let serialized = glyph_buffer.serialize(
+        &shaper,

+    );
+    println!("serialize={serialized}");
+    if let (Some(info), Some(pos)) = (infos.first(), positions.first()) {
+        let x_adv_px = (pos.x_advance as f32 / upem) * 40.0;
+        println!("x_adv_px={x_adv_px}");
+        println!("gid_u16={}", info.glyph_id as u16);
+    }
+
+    let sfont = swash::FontRef::from_index(&data, 0).expect("swash font");
+    let mut settings = Vec::<swash::Setting<f32>>::new();
+    let wght = swash::Tag::from_be_bytes(*b"wght");
+    let opsz = swash::Tag::from_be_bytes(*b"opsz");
+    if let Some(axis) = sfont.variations().find_by_tag(wght) {
+        settings.push((wght, 400.0f32.clamp(axis.min_value(), axis.max_value())).into());
+    }
+    if let Some(axis) = sfont.variations().find_by_tag(opsz) {
+        settings.push((opsz, 40.0f32.clamp(axis.min_value(), axis.max_value())).into());
+    }
+    let mut scale_context = swash::scale::ScaleContext::new();
+    let mut scaler = scale_context
+        .builder(sfont)
+        .size(40.0)
+        .hint(false)
+        .variations(settings.into_iter())
+        .build();
+    if let Some(info) = infos.first() {
+        let gid = info.glyph_id as u16;
+        if let Some(outline) = scaler.scale_outline(gid) {
+            let bounds = outline.bounds();
+            let mut used_min_x = f32::INFINITY;
+            let mut used_max_x = f32::NEG_INFINITY;
+            let mut point_i = 0usize;
+            for verb in outline.verbs() {
+                let consumed = match verb {
+                    swash::zeno::Verb::MoveTo | swash::zeno::Verb::LineTo => 1usize,
+                    swash::zeno::Verb::QuadTo => 2usize,
+                    swash::zeno::Verb::CurveTo => 3usize,
+                    swash::zeno::Verb::Close => 0usize,
+                };
+                if consumed == 0 {
+                    continue;
+                }
+                let end = point_i + consumed;
+                if let Some(slice) = outline.points().get(point_i..end) {
+                    for point in slice {
+                        used_min_x = used_min_x.min(point.x);
+                        used_max_x = used_max_x.max(point.x);
+                    }
+                }
+                point_i = end;
+            }
+            println!(
+                "outline points={} verbs={} bounds_all=({:.4},{:.4}) bounds_used=({:.4},{:.4})",
+                outline.points().len(),
+                outline.verbs().len(),
+                bounds.min.x,
+                bounds.max.x,
+                used_min_x,
+                used_max_x
+            );
+        } else {
+            println!("scale_outline returned None");
+        }
+    }
+}

  const l = eng.layoutText({ text: token, family: "Inter Variable", fontSize: 58, lineHeight: 58 * 1.2, width: null, height: null, alignH: 0, wrapMode: 0, weight: w, style: 0, axisQuantization: 1, axes: {} });
  let minX = Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY;
  let maxX = Number.NEGATIVE_INFINITY;
  for (const g of l.glyphs) {
    const ras = eng.rasterizeGlyph(g.key);
    if (!ras) continue;
    minX = Math.min(minX, g.x + ras.left);
    maxX = Math.max(maxX, g.x + ras.left + ras.width);
  }
  const rasterTight = Number.isFinite(minX) && Number.isFinite(maxX) ? Math.max(0, maxX - minX) : 0;
  console.log(JSON.stringify({
    w,
    outlineTight: Number(l.tightWidth.toFixed(1)),
    rasterTight: Number(rasterTight.toFixed(1)),
  }));
}
eng.dispose();
EOF
```
